The Arid Regions/ Deserts *Desert is a barren area of landscape where little precipitation occurs and consequently, living conditions are hostile for plant and animal. About 1/3rd of the land surface of the world is arid or semiarid. Regions receiving precipitation of less than 25 cms annually are categorized as deserts. Deserts can be classiﬁ ed by the amount of precipitation, by the temperature that prevails, by the causes of desertiﬁ cation or by their geographical location. *Tropical hot deserts are generally found in the western side of a continent between 15o to 30o north or south of the equator. Most of the major deserts of the world lie in areas crossed by the trade winds. *According to German Scientist Dr. Gerhard Knies, the amount of energy which is produced by the world deserts in 6 hours is more than the amount of energy consumed by the entire humankind in a year. Hence deserts are a very prominent source of renewable energy. *The Sahara Desert is the largest non-polar desert of the world. The desert comprises much of North Africa, excluding the fertile regions on the Mediterranean sea coast. It occupies a total area of 3600000 sq. mile. The Sahara covers large parts of Algeria, Chad, Egypt, Libya, Mauritania, Morocco, Niger, Western Sahara, Sudan and Tunisia. The main phenomena behind the formation of African and Euro-Asian deserts are – 1. Their proximity to cold ocean currents which run along the coast. These cold oceans currents cool the air and make it harder for the air to hold moisture. 2. Most of these deserts are located far away from the moisture-laden trade winds. Tropical Grasslands- These are located near the equator (10o to 25o North or South Latitudes), between the tropic of cancer and Tropic of Capricorn. The Tropical Grasslands are also known as Savannas. The Savanna grasslands are mostly found in East Africa. They are also found in Orinico basin (Venezuela and Colombia), Brazil , Honduras, Southern parts of India. These grasslands are known by diﬀ erent names in diﬀ erent parts of the world. In Africa, they are known as Savanna, Llanos in Venezuela, Campos in Brazil, and Selvas in Amazon basin. 2. Temperate Grasslands- Located between 30o to 45o North and South Latitudes. Due to greater territorial expansion in the Northern Hemisphere, these grassland (in northern hemisphere) may extend up 50o North Latitude.
